name: Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul
architect: Napoleon LeBrun; John Notman (dome and facade)
history: Bishop Francis Kenrick announced the new cathedral in 1846 and laid the cornerstone that December. To avoid debt he funded it slowly, partly by selling cemetery lots. The walls were finished and the cross raised on the dome in 1859, and the cathedral was dedicated in 1864. It became a minor basilica in 1976.
arch: Napoleon LeBrun designed the church; John Notman added the Palladian facade and dome after 1850. It is the largest Catholic church in Pennsylvania, seating about 2,000.
features: The facade is a Roman temple front with a triangular pediment.
The copper dome is topped by a lantern and cross raised in 1859.

look.d: Workers raised the cross to the top of this dome in 1859.
John Notman's Palladian facade, with columns and a pediment, was added after 1850.

fun: The bishop sold burial plots to pay for it and planned a long build to spread the cost.
journal: Philadelphia's mother church: a Roman temple front and a patient, debt-free dome.
